status: DRAFT for review (Batch 3). Maps USDA FoodData Central NAMES (plus record attributes) of the category 'Fruits and Fruit Juices' to candidate lexicon rows of kind fruit: WHOLE/SIMPLE forms only (raw, or frozen-unsweetened). Juices, concentrates, sweetened, canned, dried and prepared forms are NOT this batch. It never decides a NOVA group: FDC supplies naming evidence only; placement comes from the FAO clause.

clause.text: Fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen, or dried fruit and leafy and root vegetables
clause.where: FAO 2019 (Monteiro et al.), Table 1, Group 1 examples, p. 11 (first example of the Group 1 row)
clause.basis: inference level: class-instance of fruit; the clause names 'fruit' without listing species, and the Group 1 definition names 'edible parts of plants (fruit, seeds, leaves, stems, roots, tubers)' (same table); botanical fruit used as vegetables or berries/drupes/pomes/tropical fruit are instances of the class, none is named
clause.scope: The clause is unconditioned and names the forms fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen or dried. In THIS batch only the plain raw and the frozen-unsweetened whole/cut fruit are instances: 'squeezed' (juice) and 'dried' forms, juices, concentrates, purees, sauces, jams, canned or syrup-packed or sweetened fruit, fruit cocktails and salads, smoothies and dishes are not accepted here (juices are a CONDITIONED clause: 'fresh or pasteurized fruit or vegetable juices (with no added sugar, sweeteners or flavours)'; fruit in syrup is Group 3: 'whole fruit preserved in syrup').

acceptance: A1. The FDC food category is exactly 'Fruits and Fruit Juices'.

A2. The plain form is established by the name ('raw', or 'frozen' + 'unsweetened') OR by the record attribute: a Foundation record whose FoodOn item name states '(raw)' where the description does not.
A3. The name holds no word from the word guard, no product word and no queue word.
A4. Record attributes do not contradict the plain form (no portion descriptor holding a guard word).
A5. The derived label term is a distinct food name: else QUEUE.
A6. Canonical deduplication: cultivar, grade, colour-shade, region and cut variants of one fruit collapse into ONE row; the rest are synonym CANDIDATES (synonyms.csv is not touched).

word_guard.why: The category-wide extension of the Spices and Herbs word guard (owner rule 3): any treatment, addition, packing medium, concentrate or product word puts the name outside a plain raw or frozen-unsweetened fruit. 'unsweetened' is NOT guarded (it is the clause-compatible frozen form; 'sweetened' is). 'Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program' is a programme note and is removed before the check.

product_words.why: A juice, powder, flour, puree, sauce, jam, cocktail, salad or smoothie of fruit is a product, not the fruit: REJECT. Raisins, prunes and dates are DRIED fruit: dried forms are per-term only (dehydrated-policy-1), routed to the owner.

queue_words.dried: dried forms: the clause names 'dried' but earlier owner policy (dehydrated-policy-1) keeps dried/dehydrated forms per-term only.
queue_words.peel: a plant-part variant (peel, rind) of a fruit: not established as a label term.
queue_words.rind: a plant-part variant (rind) of a fruit.
queue_words.olives: olives are eaten brined or processed; the raw fruit is not a label term and FAO Group 3 names preserved fruit; QUEUE.
queue_words.carob: not a fruit example of the clause; no source read places it.
queue_words.roselle: calyces used as a hibiscus herb/tea; not established as a fruit term.
queue_words.tamarinds: tamarind is a culinary pulp/sourcing ingredient on Indian labels (tamarind pulp, paste): the raw fruit name is queued until the pulp/paste forms are decided (owner).
queue_words.coconut: coconut is a nut/seed in this project's vocabulary (Nut and Seed batch).
